problem_statement: The MQTT-5 input property decoders take each property's length from the received packet. When the bytes of a property section arrive incomplete relative to what its lengths declare, a property whose declared length exceeds the bytes actually received must be rejected, and a well-formed property whose declared length fits within the received bytes must be accepted and fully consumed. The observable misbehavior is that a property whose declared length overruns the received input is nevertheless accepted and consumed instead of being rejected, across the UTF-8 string, fixed-length integer, binary data, UTF-8 string pair, and variable byte integer property types. This includes a binary data property whose declared length is 259 bytes but for which only a few bytes follow: that over-long property is still accepted. Well-formed properties of each type continue to be accepted and fully consumed.

superseded_statements.problem_statement: The MQTT-5 input property decoders validate a property only against the destination buffer size (MQTT_PROP_MAX_PROP_LENGTH), never against the bytes actually received, so a property whose declared length overruns the received input reads past the end of the input. In the worst case decode_prop_utf8_pair() reads buf_in[len1+2] (len1 taken from the packet) before any bounds check, and decode_prop_binary_data() truncated its 16-bit length into a uint8_t. The decoders must thread the available input length (bounded by payload_pos) and reject a property whose declared length exceeds it.
check_issues: `problem_statement` names code of the fix that the tests do not use (MQTT_PROP_MAX_PROP_LENGTH, decode_prop_binary_data, decode_prop_utf8_pair); describe what a caller observes instead

causal_chain: The test places a property section into the connection's input buffer and sets the received-byte boundary to fewer bytes than the full property, decodes the section, walks every property, and compares the consumed byte count against the expected result. For each property type it feeds both a well-formed property (expecting full consumption) and one whose declared length overruns the received bytes (expecting rejection, PROP_REJECTED). Before the fix the over-long property is accepted, so the consumed count differs from PROP_REJECTED and the assertions fail. After the fix the over-long declared length is rejected, the binary-data over-long case is rejected, and the well-formed cases still fully consume, so the assertions pass.

verification.reason: The statement describes the overrun bug but omits the observable post-rejection parse behavior and several incomplete-input edge cases that the hidden tests require; these can be added as requirements without revealing the implementation.

problems.detail: The hidden test checks that a rejected property advances the parse position only past its property identifier, so a rejected single-byte property identifier consumes exactly one byte; the statement only says the property must be rejected and does not specify the observable consumption.

The statement is ambiguous about whether rejection means the whole property section is abandoned or only the individual property is skipped; the test requires the section to remain present and the rejected property to be not consumed further.

The test checks rejection when a length prefix, continuation bits, or the second length prefix/string of a pair is missing, not only when a fully decoded length overruns; the statement does not make these incomplete-input cases explicit.

leak_check.leak_detail: The phrase 'not only when a fully decoded length overruns the received bytes' hints at an implementation condition rather than only stating the required observable behavior, but it is not essential and can be removed.
leak_check.suggested_statement: The MQTT-5 input property decoders take each property's length from the received packet. When the bytes of a property section arrive incomplete relative to what its lengths declare, a property whose declared length exceeds the bytes actually received must be rejected, and a well-formed property whose declared length fits within the received bytes must be accepted and fully consumed. The observable misbehavior is that a property whose declared length overruns the received input is nevertheless accepted and consumed instead of being rejected, across the UTF-8 string, fixed-length integer, binary data, UTF-8 string pair, and variable byte integer property types. This includes a binary data property whose declared length is 259 bytes but for which only a few bytes follow: that over-long property was incorrectly accepted in the misbehavior. Well-formed properties of each type continue to be accepted and fully consumed. Rejection must also apply when a required length field or a variable byte integer is not fully present in the received input. For a rejected property, the property identifier is still consumed but the property value is not; when the property identifier is a single byte, this means the rejected property consumes one byte. An accepted property consumes its entire encoded length. Rejection of a malformed property does not make the property section absent.
